name: Puppet, Inc. (formerly Puppet Labs; owned by Perforce)
origin_detail: Founded 2005 in Portland, Oregon, by Luke Kanies around his open-source Puppet configuration tool; acquired by Perforce Software in 2022
openness_notes: Puppet began as a GPLv2 open-source tool sold with services; from v2.7.0 it moved to Apache-2.0 while Puppet Enterprise became the proprietary paid product (open core). In early 2025 Perforce moved official binaries/packages to a private repository under an EULA (free only up to 25 nodes for non-commercial/dev use) and slowed public source commits; the source stays Apache-2.0, so the rating is 2, but practical openness fell sharply and the community forked it (OpenVox).

license_history.license: Apache-2.0 source; official binaries in a private repository under EULA; >25 nodes requires commercial licence
license_history.note: Announced by Perforce in Nov 2024, effective early 2025

relicensing_events.outcome_note: Permissive relicence alongside the launch of proprietary Puppet Enterprise; year approximate

relicensing_events.from: Public Apache-2.0 binaries and frequent public commits
relicensing_events.to: EULA-gated official binaries (25-node limit) and slowed public commits
relicensing_events.fork_backer: Vox Pupuli community (Puppet module maintainers); Perforce refused use of the Puppet name
relicensing_events.outcome_note: Not a change to the source licence. Community declared 'Perforce is forking Puppet'; universities such as NC State announced a move to OpenVox in Jul 2025

exit_events.note: Announced Apr 2022, closed May 2022; price undisclosed; Perforce then laid off ~15% of Puppet's Portland workforce

risk_events: Competition from agentless and cloud-native tools reduced Puppet's market position before its sale (not quantified in fetched pages)
2022: sold to Perforce (a PE-backed consolidator) for an undisclosed price; ~15% layoffs in Portland

Nov 2024/early 2025: binaries moved behind an EULA with a 25-node limit; last open-source Puppet release 8.10 (22 Oct 2024); community fork OpenVox (Vox Pupuli, first release 21 Jan 2025); institutions migrating (e.g. NC State, Aug 2025)
robustness: The Apache-2.0 code base survives via the OpenVox fork, which keeps a fully open build. The company is now a product line inside Perforce, with no independent valuation, revenue or headcount disclosed, and community goodwill was damaged by the 2025 restrictions.
physical_science_relevance: Puppet has been widely used to manage HPC clusters and university research computing fleets (e.g. NC State's move to OpenVox), so the 2025 restrictions directly affected research IT.
openness_effect_assessment: Openness built Puppet's early dominance in configuration management and raised $150M, but the open-core model did not deliver an IPO-scale outcome; after a quiet sale to Perforce, the new owner restricted the community distribution, and the community forked. The closing protected Perforce's licence revenue at the cost of the user base's trust.
key_takeaway: Puppet follows the post-acquisition closing pattern: a once-leading open-source DevOps tool, bought by a consolidator, then restricted (EULA-gated binaries, 25-node limit) in 2025, prompting a community fork (OpenVox) that research institutions adopted. Ownership change, not the founders, drove the closing.
